g.text: Words on this sheet
user space / kernel space — two privilege levels of the CPU: programs run in user space and
must ask the kernel to touch hardware
system call — a function call into the kernel (open, read, write, ioctl …); the CPU switches
into kernel mode to run it
ioctl — "I/O control": a system call for device-specific requests, each identified by a
number (a "request code")
driver — kernel code that knows how to operate one kind of hardware (registers, interrupts)
subsystem — a generic kernel layer for one kind of device (gpiolib for GPIO, I2C core …)
that drivers plug into
device tree / compatible — the board's hardware description (.dtb). Each node's "compatible"
string is how the kernel picks its driver
probe() — the driver function the kernel calls when it matches a device; it sets the
hardware up and registers it
register — a memory address inside a chip block that controls or reports hardware (e.g.
PMIC — power-management chip: makes the board's supply voltages (the TPS65217 on the
BeagleBone)
hwmon — the kernel's framework for monitoring sensors (temperatures, voltages …):
/sys/class/hwmon
cpsw / musb / MMC — the AM335x's Ethernet, USB and SD/eMMC controllers (and their drivers)
struct gpio_chip — the "table of functions" a GPIO driver fills in so gpiolib can call it
